newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 21 pct-Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Feb palm oil output seen down 21 pct-Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in February is expected to fall by 21 percent to 455,000 tonnes from January, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Wednesday.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of February at 595,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 696,272 tonnes at end-January.
Exports in February are estimated at between 465,000 and 470,000 tonnes against 551,665 tonnes in January, he said.
Wong said in a report that partial data for first half February showed production declines ranging from down from 20-25 pct when compared to the first half of January.

He said harvesters/millers had started to clear the backlog since late last week. "At the moment, it is uncertain whether the backlog could be fully cleared by the end of this month as some producing areas, especially those in Sabah and Sarawak, had widespread rains for several days.
Wong added that tight supplies and poor margins for refineries would curtail exports further this month. Improved supplies in March are, however, likely to result in a strong recovery in shipments.
